facts.claim: Called 'Austria's Mona Lisa'; displayed at the Belvedere, Vienna, from 1941 to 2006
In 1941 the Nazi lawyer Erich Führer delivered it to the gallery with a note saying it was given according to Adele's wishes, signed 'Heil Hitler'
Maria Altmann (born 18 Feb 1916) filed a claim in 1998, aged 82, with lawyer Randol Schoenberg
Adele Bauer (b. 9 Aug 1881) married Ferdinand Bloch (b. 1864) on 19 Dec 1899; her sister had married his brother; two prominent Jewish families; names combined to Bloch-Bauer
Adele hosted a renowned Viennese salon; she knew Klimt from the late 1890s
Summer 1903: Ferdinand commissioned the portrait as an anniversary present for Adele's parents in October; Klimt was slow and it was finished in 1907
More than one hundred preparatory drawings survive
December 1903: Klimt visited San Vitale, Ravenna, and admired its sixth-century Byzantine mosaics, especially Empress Theodora before a gold background: 'mosaics of unprecedented splendor'
Oil, silver and gold on canvas, with raised (gesso) relief patterns; oil only for face and hands
The Neue Galerie says it is unclear whether she is standing or seated
Adele had a disfigured finger from a childhood accident; Frank Whitford reads the hand position as hiding it (disputed)
Critics divided; the Neues Wiener Tagblatt: 'Mehr Blech als Bloch' (more brass than Bloch)
An unprecedented second commission, completed in 1912 (Adele Bloch-Bauer II)
Klimt died of a stroke in early February 1918, aged 55
Adele's 1923 will: 'I ask my husband after his death to leave my two portraits and the four landscapes by Gustav Klimt to the Austrian State Gallery in Vienna'
Adele died of meningitis on 24 January 1925, aged 43; her room with the Klimts was kept as a memorial; Ferdinand assured the probate court he would honour her wish
9 Dec 1937 Maria married Fritz Altmann; Ferdinand gave her Adele's diamond necklace; the Gestapo confiscated it in June 1938
Bruno Walter's live Vienna Philharmonic recording of Mahler's Ninth, 16 January 1938, weeks before the Anschluss; Walter had to flee

Fritz Altmann was sent to Dachau to force his brother to hand over the family textile business; the couple fled on foot into the Netherlands, guided by a farmer across a brook and under barbed wire; via Liverpool to the US; Maria sold clothes from her home in Los Angeles
Ferdinand fled to Czechoslovakia, then Switzerland; the Nazis seized his estate (sugar factory, castle, Klimt paintings) on false tax-evasion charges
1941: Führer traded the portrait (and Apple Tree I) to the Belvedere for Kammer Castle on the Attersee III, sold to Gustav Ucicky
Ucicky directed Nazi propaganda films (Heimkehr, 1941) and is believed to be Klimt's son
Renamed 'Dame in Gold' (Lady in Gold) to remove its Jewish subject
Ferdinand died in Switzerland on 13 Nov 1945, nearly destitute; his last will left his estate to his nephew and two nieces, including Maria
1946 Annulment Act; in 1948 the heirs were told the will gave the Belvedere title and gave up the Klimt claims; export permits were conditioned on leaving art to museums
Provenance records were later falsified to suggest the portraits were acquired before the Nazi invasion
1998 Art Restitution Law opened the archives; Hubertus Czernin found documents showing Ferdinand had not donated the paintings, and the 'Heil Hitler' letter
Ferdinand owned the paintings; Adele's will was a non-binding request (arbitral award)
Schoenberg: grandson of Arnold Schoenberg; his grandmother was Maria's best friend
1999: committee rejected the claim citing the will; Austrian court fees proportional to value, over US$1.5 million; she sued in Los Angeles
Republic of Austria v. Altmann, 541 U.S. 677, decided 7 June 2004, 6-3 (Stevens): FSIA applies, she could sue
Binding arbitration in Austria (three arbitrators); January 2006 award: five paintings to the heirs, including both portraits
Maria said she'd like the portraits to stay in Austria; the government said it could not afford about $300 million
'Ciao Adele' posters across Vienna
Left Austria March 2006; shown at LACMA April-June 2006; June 2006 Ronald Lauder bought it for the Neue Galerie for $135 million, a record; Lauder called it 'our Mona Lisa'
Maria Altmann died at home in Los Angeles on 7 Feb 2011, aged 94; the 2015 film Woman in Gold starred Helen Mirren

titles: The True Story Behind Woman in Gold
The Nazis Renamed Her. Her Niece Took Her Back.
youtube.description_lead: In 1903 a Viennese sugar industrialist asked Gustav Klimt to paint his wife, Adele Bloch-Bauer. Four years and more than a hundred drawings later, Klimt delivered the golden portrait that became his masterpiece. In 1941 a Nazi lawyer handed it to Austria's national gallery with a letter signed 'Heil Hitler', and the gallery renamed it 'The Lady in Gold'. For sixty years it was Austria's Mona Lisa, until Adele's niece Maria Altmann, a refugee in Los Angeles, took the Republic of Austria all the way to the United States Supreme Court. This is the true story behind the film Woman in Gold.
